english_translation: The sun has come out brightly today; the clothes are drying quickly.

dialogue.shona: Zuva ranyatsobuda nhasi; mbatya dziri kuoma nekukurumidza.
dialogue.english: The sun has come out brightly today; the clothes are drying quickly.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Zuva [sun / day] • ranyatsobuda [ranyatsobuda] • nhasi [today] • mbatya [clothes] • dziri [dziri] • kuoma [to / at oma] • nekukurumidza [quickly / rapidly]

grammar_notes.title: Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nekukurumidza'
grammar_notes.content: Look closely at 'nekukurumidza'. In Shona, the word for 'and' or 'with' between nouns is not a separate word—instead, the prefix 'ne-' (or 'na-' before people's names) is written attached directly to the second noun! For example, 'ne-' + 'kukurumidza' forms 'nekukurumidza'. You will see this everywhere in daily speech: 'sadza nemuriwo' ('sadza and vegetables'), 'nesimba' ('with strength'), and 'nekukasira' ('with haste / quickly').
grammar_notes.rule: ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

grammar_notes.title: Infinitive Verbs & Action Nouns with 'ku-' ('nekukurumidza')
grammar_notes.content: Look at 'nekukurumidza' in this sentence. Every Shona verb in its dictionary ('to do') form begins with 'ku-': for example, 'kudya' (to eat), 'kutenga' (to buy), 'kubhadhara' (to pay), 'kuona' (to see), and 'kurwa' (to fight). Because 'ku-' verbs also behave as action nouns ('eating', 'paying', 'working'), you can attach linking prefixes directly to them: 'yekubhadhara' ('for paying'), 'pakubikwa' ('in the cooking'), and 'nekuona' ('by/with seeing').
grammar_notes.rule: ku- + Verb Stem = 'to [verb] / [verb]-ing' (ku- + -tenga = kutenga, 'to buy'; ye- + kubhadhara = yekubhadhara, 'for paying')

grammar_notes.title: Describing How Actions Are Done: Adverbs & Intensifiers ('nekukurumidza')
grammar_notes.content: To describe HOW an action is performed, Shona frequently uses the prefix 'zva-' / 'zvi-' or intensifiers like 'nekukurumidza'. Compare these high-frequency expressions you will hear every day: 'zvakanaka' ('well / nicely'), 'zvakasimba' ('firmly / strongly'), 'zvishoma' ('a little bit'), 'zvinyoronyoro' ('gently / softly'), and 'chaizvo' or 'zvikuru' ('very much / davvero').
grammar_notes.rule: Verb + Adverb of Manner/Degree (zvakanaka = well, zvakasimba = firmly, zvishoma = a little, chaizvo/zvikuru = very much)

cultural_notes.title: Zimbabwe's Abundant Sunshine ('Zuva') & Line-Drying Laundry
cultural_notes.content: With over 3,000 hours of bright sunshine a year across Zimbabwe, clothes washed in the morning and hung outside dry crisp and fresh in a matter of hours ('mbatya dziri kuoma nekukurumidza') whenever the sun comes out ('zuva ranyatsobuda').

active_exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'The girl is wearing a yellow hat and a blue dress'?
options: Musikana akapfeka ngowani yeyero nerokwe rebhuruu.
Mukomana akapfeka bhachi dema neshangu tsvuku.
Mbatya dzose dziri kuoma pamutambo panze.
active_exercises.correct_answer: Musikana akapfeka ngowani yeyero nerokwe rebhuruu.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ngowani yeyero' = 'a yellow hat', and 'nerokwe rebhuruu' = 'and a blue dress'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Ndeipi shangu yaunoda, nhema kana tsvuku?'
options: Where did you put my white shirt and blue trousers?
Which shoe do you want, the black one or the red one?
These new shoes are very comfortable for walking.
She washed all the white clothes this morning.
active_exercises.correct_answer: Which shoe do you want, the black one or the red one?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ndeipi shangu yaunoda' = 'Which shoe do you want', 'nhema kana tsvuku' = 'the black one or the red one'.

active_exercises.prompt: In 'Shiri diki dziri kuimba pamusoro pemuti', what are the small birds doing?
options: Singing at the top of the tree
Looking for seeds in the field
active_exercises.correct_answer: Singing at the top of the tree
active_exercises.explanation: 'Shiri diki' = 'small birds', 'dziri kuimba' = 'are singing', 'pamusoro pemuti' = 'at the top of the tree'.
